title: Agentic Enterprise - What your CEO must know about AI -  Hubert Misztela
talk_summary: Hubert Misztela argues that agentic workflows matter because LLMs can handle cognitive steps and glue tasks together, so companies should map workflows, context, and personas before deploying agents. He also urges democratized agent-building, persistent organizational memory, and explicit human/agent task splits, with little concrete implementation detail or measured evidence.

takeaways.what_they_do: They recommend identifying each workflow and capturing the exact context: data used, systems touched, transformations, and decision conditions, because this often lives only in employees' heads.
takeaways.evidence_quote: identify your workflows right then you need to understand the exact context around them

takeaways.what_they_do: They suggest routing ambiguous, situation-dependent, or subjective steps to humans, while repetitive and tedious steps are better executed by agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: ambiguous workflows where a lot depends upon the situation and it's not clear how to define it, obviously it's going to be better executed by humans

takeaways.what_they_do: They propose digital-twin-like memory so expertise and prior decisions can be retained and queried after employees leave or contexts change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: digital twins like time travelers and memory to retain the uh organizational knowledge

takeaways.technique: Shared workflow agents instead of per-person agents
takeaways.what_they_do: They describe agents serving not just one employee but the whole team or workflow, which reduces duplicated individual assistants.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents serving not only one employee but the whole team or the whole workflow

takeaways.technique: Agents build routines on the spot
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue employees should be able to build agents quickly with low-code or coding assistants after making their own hidden steps explicit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: building the agents on the spot

takeaways.what_they_do: They suggest analyzing contributors as personas/archetypes to find repeated patterns across workflows, then optimizing shared agent opportunities.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there is a certain pattern repeating in two different workflows then you can optimize for those two workflows
